summary: Reductions, scans and cross-worker merge semantics implemented through the real compilation path. (1) a100c/plan/stages.py: the reduction operation table as data (13 constructs, per-op-and-dtype identities derived from the lattice of the type's own signedness -- a signed min reduces from INT_MAX, an unsigned min from all-ones, fp max from -inf; declared tie-breaks, empty-extent results, merge rules), the two-phase cross-worker split plan (single-program grids: worker-strided chunk ranges, partials to owned workspace slots, one a100rt_stage_barrier per worker per call, merge owner worker 0 combining under the source's own semantics), loop-carried reduction recognition (accumulate + arg-select pair forms), workspace ownership (disjoint per-worker regions, violating plans rejected), and the SplitKFeed model for the dot lane. (2) TIR: reduce/scan/sort/topk/histogram ops carrying kind, axes, keep_dims, identity and tie-break, with verifier rules (wrong identity, out-of-range axis, wrong result shape, non-index index-form each rejected; identities checked against the plan table). (3) Frontend: tl.sum/max/min/argmax/argmin (return_indices, tie_break_left), xor_sum, reduce_or, cumsum, cumprod, sort, topk, histogram lower to those ops (pinned promotions: int<32 -> 32-bit, bf16 -> fp32 for max/min forms); tl.softmax refuses with a located diagnostic naming its exp dependency; tl.cast folds the identity cast and emits convert otherwise; multi-result (value,index) tuple unpacking; runtime tuple pack/unpack. (4) Backend: vred (vredsum/max/maxu/min/minu/xor/or/vfredusum/vfredmax/vfredmin), vmv.x.s (vextract), vmand.mm, vfdiv.vv, vfcvt.f.x.v and the fp vx forms as repertoire rows; MIR opcodes + type rules + region consistency. (5) Lowering: intra-program RVV reductions per chunk (vred against the identity splat, index forms via match-masking and an index vred), chunk-merge accumulators riding the chunk loop back edge (sum/min/max/xor/or/product and (value,index) pairs with tie-break-left), scans through the worker-private workspace with a carried prefix, the two-phase split path (worker-strided chunk loop, partial stores to owned slots, stage barrier, merge loop over workers, suffix on the merge owner), masked load with other= (masked load + select), scalar float arithmetic/compares through the vector path, int32->fp32 conversion, float scalar argument bindings. Fixed five pre-existing defects this path exposed: tl.where/ifexp literal-branch order inversion, non-commutative binop literal-order inversion (n-1 became 1-n, n//2 became 2//n), padded-singleton broadcast flag at equal extent-1 targets, i32 scalar args bound to i64 registers, and the allocator's group-span interference (an m1 value landing inside an m2 neighbour's group); extended the emitter's parallel-move cycle breaking to vectors (save-dst through a free register). All executed evidence under the declared QEMU endpoint with the cases' own comparison policies.

tl.sort/tl.topk/tl.histogram lower to TIR ops with declared semantics but refuse at the lowering: whole-block reordering and k-extent/multi-shape output blocks need the layout lane's (T012) block-materialization protocol; their corpus files are additionally blocked by flip/gather/.to.

The interleaved form (a scalar store of a reduction result positioned before a later block-level statement) refuses with a located diagnostic naming the multi-region boundary; the compute-then-store form (ranked_distribution's actual shape after its other blockers clear) will need a close-and-reopen chunk-region design.

Multi-program grids with fewer programs than workers (1 < program_count < worker_count) keep the normal strided path with idle workers; extending the two-phase split to per-program worker groups is follow-up work.
Reverse scans (cumsum/cumprod reverse=True) refuse with a located diagnostic (a second pass over the block is needed); keep_dims reductions refuse (extent-1 multi-shape blocks).
